sections.content: Use *¿Quieres* + infinitive? to invite someone: *¿Quieres venir a la fiesta?* You know *querer* and *poder* from Unit 10, so you can also ask *¿Puedes* + infinitive? to check that the person is free: *¿Puedes venir el sábado?* To accept, say *Sí, claro* and add *Quiero ir* or *Puedo ir*. Keep the invitation focused on the event, time or activity. A third, more polite way is the fixed phrase *¿Te gustaría* + infinitive? (Would you like to …?), answered *Sí, me gustaría*. Learn it as a set phrase for now: in Unit 26 you will see how its verb form works.

items.english: Do you want to come to the party?
Yes, of course. I want to go.
Yes, of course. I can go.
Would you like to come to the dinner?
Yes, I would like that very much.

rows: Would you like to …? (a set phrase)

sections.content: *¿Quieres venir?* asks whether the person wants to come; *¿Puedes venir?* asks whether they are free; *¿Te gustaría venir?* is the most polite. *Sí, claro* answers all three, and *Sí, me gustaría* answers *¿Te gustaría…?*.
